bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Ethanol volume dependency on government blending policy (20%→25%); regulatory delays in RTD/tequila approvals; premium brand adoption lag in new states; packaging cost volatility; competition from Bacardi Breezer in RTD and established players in single malt
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, long-term oriented; clear focus on proprietary brands, operational control, and premiumization; transparent about challenges (ethanol, tequila delays); proactive on backward integration
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: SDF acquisition is not just about capacity—it’s a strategic geographic play (central Kerala location, proximity to airports) to solve bottling fragmentation and enable faster SKU rollout; single malt maturation already underway with blending exceeding expectations; ENA surplus is being cannibalized for own IMFL use, reducing external malt purchases
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash balance sheet: net debt/equity of (0.09)x in FY26 versus a peer group at 0.13x, with interest coverage of 23x against peers at 11x.
- Growth explicitly to be funded by internal accruals and a strong balance sheet with minimal debt, rather than fresh leverage.
- Ethanol plant debt on a defined amortisation schedule - Rs 200 Mn per year through FY26-27 and Rs 96 Mn in FY27-28.
- Gross block scaled from Rs 1,868 Mn (FY23) to Rs 5,507 Mn (FY26) while ROCE/ROE stayed at 19%/13% in FY26; net working capital days at 35 in FY26.
- Dividend outflow modest at Rs 36 Mn in FY26 (flat YoY), with Rs 888 Mn raised from share warrants in FY26 supporting the expansion programme.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated presence across the entire liquor value chain — IMFL (proprietary and licensed), IMIL, ENA and ethanol — from a single location described as India's largest integrated manufacturing facility
- Scale of the Barwaha complex: 41 bottling lines with a collective 16 million cases per annum, 53 MLPA ENA and 43 MLPA ethanol capacity
- Portfolio of 16 proprietary brands alongside an IMFL franchise arrangement with Diageo and contract manufacturing for United Spirits Limited (Diageo) and Inbrew
- Backward integration strengthened by the newly commissioned 6,000 LPD malt spirit plant, positioning the Company for the premium and single malt whisky segment
- Product innovation credential — accredited as the first in the world to manufacture white brandy
- Proprietary IMFL momentum — proprietary brand revenues grew approximately 29% and proprietary IMFL volumes grew 32% during the year, reflecting brand acceptance across key markets
- Participation in the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme diversifies revenue streams beyond beverage alcohol
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- State-controlled regulatory regime for alcohol — The MD&A's Industry Structure section notes the industry is strictly governed by state laws on production, distribution and marketing; licences and permits are required for manufacturing, bottling, storage, distribution and retail, and states may control distribution through government-owned entities or allow private distributors. Any change in a state's excise policy or licensing regime directly affects the Company's route to market.
- Excise duty structure and the new 40% GST demerit rate on sin goods — High inter-state duties prevail, requiring manufacturers to have multiple manufacturing units in different states of operation — a structural cost of geographic expansion. GST rate rationalisation introduced in September 2025 created a two-tier 5%/18% structure alongside a newly introduced 40% demerit rate for luxury and sin goods, raising the tax burden on the category.
- Advertising and distribution restrictions limit brand-building levers — Advertising restrictions, particularly above-the-line (ATL) advertising, limit marketing efforts, while hyper-local or on-demand online delivery is approved only in certain zones where state rules permit and online sales remain broadly restricted — constraining how a premiumisation strategy can be marketed and distributed.
- GLP-1 medications and changing consumption behaviour as a structural volume headwind — The MD&A explicitly flags GLP-1 drugs as creating 'an unexpected structural headwind for the alcohol industry' because they reduce alcohol cravings alongside food appetite; combined with Gen Z's more selective relationship with alcohol, this is described as a hurdle for alcohol volume growth, forcing reliance on premiumisation and low-alcohol launches to hold value.
- Input cost inflation and raw material availability from geopolitical supply-chain disruption — The Middle East war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz produced an energy crisis and severe supply chain disruptions; the FY 2026-27 outlook cites a sharp rise in crude oil prices and disrupted energy supply 'putting pressure on input costs and raw material availability'. Global headline inflation is projected to rise to 4.4% in 2026 with surging production and freight costs.
- Agricultural / monsoon dependence and rural demand — The Company's grain-based distillation depends on agricultural inputs, and the outlook states a deficient south-west monsoon is expected to impact agricultural activity and rural demand — a dual hit to grain cost and to the IMIL segment that primarily caters to the low-income rural segment.
- Open competition-law proceedings (CCI investigation into IMIL supply) — The Board's Report discloses that the CCI's Director General searched the registered office on 27 October 2021 to examine the supply and sale of IMIL products, and that a CCI order alleged cartelisation in IMIL supply; by order dated 20 March 2024 the CCI referred the investigation report back to the DG for further investigation, leaving the matter unresolved.
- Cybersecurity and digital infrastructure risk — The Board's Report describes mitigations — firewall systems, genuine software applications, regular hardware updates, up-to-date antivirus solutions, employee training on cybersecurity best practices, a disaster recovery mechanism and a Digital Rights Management system — which identifies cyber threats to digital infrastructure as a risk management sees as live.
- Concentration of manufacturing at a single integrated complex — Production is centred on the integrated Barwaha manufacturing complex, where the new 6,000 LPD Malt Spirit Plant and the 130 KLPD grain-based ethanol plant sit; with high inter-state duties separately noted as requiring multiple units across states, single-site dependence is both an operating-disruption exposure and a limit on market access.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Present across the entire liquor value chain - IMFL Proprietary, IMFL Licensed, IMIL, Merchant ENA and Ethanol - with by-products (cattle feed) monetised alongside, described as the largest integrated manufacturing facility at a single location.
- Two decades of partnership with Diageo and status as one of only four exclusive Diageo contract manufacturing partners; also contract manufactures for Inbrew, giving a captive B2B volume base.
- Dominant IMFL footprint in Madhya Pradesh and Keralam, where it is a top-3 private player with ~1.5% market share (FY26) and was the fastest to reach 1 million cases in under four years after 2018 entry.
- Centrally located in the heart of India, giving equidistant access to raw-material mandis and distribution hubs across the country; claims to be the first company in the world to make White Brandy (Lemount).
- Present in 14 states/UTs including MP, Chhattisgarh, Keralam, Delhi, West Bengal, UP, Maharashtra, Goa, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Manipur and Odisha.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] SDF Industries acquired via an IBC resolution plan approved by NCLT Kochi on 16 April 2026 for Rs 30.85 Cr; it becomes a wholly owned subsidiary and brings Kerala bottling in-house.
- [Business model change] The Inbrew arrangement shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing, structurally reducing reported IMFL licensed volumes without an equivalent economic loss.
- [Segment headwind] Ethanol faces industry oversupply that management expects to persist for the rest of the financial year, and the segment reported an operating loss in Q1FY27.
- [Industry] Indian alco-bev market sized at INR 3,255 Bn in 2024 heading to INR 5,763 Bn by 2030P; premium & luxury alco-bev at INR 28,751 Cr in 2024 to INR 50,000 Cr by 2029E, with whisky over 70% of IMFL.
- [Leadership] Promoter-led board (Prasann Kumar Kedia MD, Anshuman Kedia WTD & CEO) supplemented by senior hires from Pernod Ricard India and United Spirits in sales and marketing.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: AABL manufactures across the entire liquor value chain — Indian Made Foreign Liquor (both proprietary and licensed), Indian Made Indian Liquor, Extra Neutral Alcohol, ethanol and malt spirit — from an integrated complex at Barwaha near Indore, Madhya Pradesh. It crafts premium whisky, vodka, gin, brandy, rum, RTD and ENA, sells 16 proprietary brands, operates as an IMFL franchisee for Diageo and undertakes contract manufacturing for United Spirits Limited (Diageo) and Inbrew. Its footprint spans twelve states with a stated long-term strategy of becoming a pan-India integrated alcoholic beverage player.

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: RTD (Kultur) soft-launched in MP, label approvals pending in 14 states; tequila launch delayed to H1 FY27 due to shipping; single malt to launch H2 FY28 (FY29 full year); expansion into Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka; target 50% revenue from proprietary IMFL in 3-5 years
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Remain focused on enhancing operational efficiency, expanding the market footprint, building proprietary brands and investing in strategic growth initiatives
- Grow the proprietary IMFL business — proprietary brand revenues grew approximately 29% and proprietary IMFL volumes 32% during the year on increasing brand acceptance
- Expand and strengthen the portfolio through focused investments in premium and value-added offerings across whisky, gin, vodka, rum and brandy
- Deepen backward integration via the commissioned 6,000 LPD Malt Spirit Plant at Barwaha, positioning the Company to participate in the premium and single malt whisky segment in the coming years
- Build a pan-India integrated alcoholic beverage business — footprint already across Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Goa, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, West Bengal and Manipur, with foundations laid for Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka
- Diversify revenue streams through the grain-based 130 KLPD ethanol plant at Barwaha, supporting the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme and participation in the renewable energy ecosystem
- Expand IMFL bottling capacity inorganically — acquisition of SDF Industries Limited, Kerala through the IBC resolution process, making it a wholly owned subsidiary
- Shift certain franchise arrangements to a contract manufacturing / job work model, trading reported revenue for improved business mix and operational efficiency
- Embed sustainability across the value chain in support of a long-term vision of responsible growth and enhanced stakeholder trust
- Maintain focus on operational excellence, governance and stakeholder value creation alongside continued investment in manufacturing capabilities, product innovation, premiumization, market expansion and strategic partnerships
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: AABL's expansion during FY 2025-26 centred on its integrated complex at Barwaha, near Indore, Madhya Pradesh — described as the country's largest integrated manufacturing facility at a single location. The headline project was the successful commissioning and stabilisation of a state-of-the-art Malt Spirit Plant of 6,000 LPD capacity at Barwaha, which strengthened backward integration and positioned the Company to participate in the premium and single malt whisky segment in the coming years; the Directors' Report attributes the year's higher depreciation to this Malt Plant being commissioned during the year. The grain-based Ethanol Plant of 130 KLPD capacity at Barwaha continued commercial operations, diversifying revenue streams and supporting the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme. The site also carries an ENA manufacturing capacity of 53 million litres per annum, an ethanol manufacturing capacity of 43 MLPA and 41 bottling lines with a collective capacity of 16 million cases per annum. Inorganically, the Company acted as Resolution Applicant in the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of SDF Industries Limited, Kerala; the resolution plan was approved by the Committee of Creditors and then by the NCLT Kochi Bench by order dated 16.04.2026, making SDF Industries a wholly owned subsidiary with the stated objective of expanding IMFL bottling capacity. Geographically, the footprint was extended across Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Goa, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, West Bengal and Manipur, with foundations laid for future growth in Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka in support of a pan-India integrated alcoholic beverage strategy. No rupee capex quantum is stated in the narrative chapters, and the named capital-commitment and segment-capital-expenditure disclosures supplied carried no readable figure with a printed unit.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Premiumization is the structural driver — consumers are trading up from mass-market to prestige, premium and luxury offerings on rising disposable incomes, urbanization, global exposure and social media influence
- Formalisation of the industry — the organized sector now controls approximately two-thirds of the Indian alcobev market by value, attributed to premiumization, stricter compliance, digital traceability and the exit of weaker informal players
- Headroom from low consumption — India's per capita alcohol consumption is nearly 5.5 litres against a global average of 6.2 litres; the Indian alcobev market was valued at $68.49 Billion in 2025 and is expected to reach $131 Billion by 2035 at 6.7% CAGR
- RTD and low-ABV formats gaining share — FSSAI amendments of 1 January 2026 formally recognised RTD as a category, easing regulatory approvals for low-ABV products and encouraging pre-mixed cocktail launches; nitro-infused beers were also assigned formal standards
- New consumer cohorts — a rising female consumer base, changing social norms and experiential/cocktail culture broadening the addressable occasion set
- Emerging distribution channels — home delivery and e-commerce gaining traction where state rules permit, though online sales remain broadly restricted
- GLP-1 medications are a structural headwind to alcohol volume growth as they reduce alcohol cravings; combined with Gen Z's more selective relationship with alcohol, players are countering through premiumization and low-alcohol launches
- Regulatory and tax structure remains the key constraint — state-specific excise regimes, exclusion of liquor from GST, high inter-state duties requiring multiple manufacturing units, ATL advertising restrictions, and a newly introduced 40% GST demerit rate for luxury and sin goods introduced in September 2025
- Macro outlook turning less supportive — India's real GDP growth is projected to decline to 6.6% in FY 2026-27 on Middle East war risk, with a sharp rise in crude prices, supply chain disruption pressuring input costs and raw material availability, and a deficient south-west monsoon expected to hit agricultural activity and rural demand
- Global growth is projected to slow to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 with headline inflation rising to 4.4% in 2026, pressuring production and freight costs
- Export optionality for Indian alcobev — APEDA targets scaling India's alcoholic beverage exports from ₹3,162.21 Crore to ₹8,535 Crore by 2030, though India currently ranks 40th worldwide in such exports
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: AABL shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing in IMFL, driving 32% YoY volume growth in proprietary brands despite flattish top line; the strategic focus on proprietary portfolio, new product launches (RTD, tequila, single malt), and acquisition of SDF Industries to control bottling is positioning it as a future-ready premium alco-bev player with 50% revenue target from own brands in 5 years.

currentContext.expansion: AABL's expansion during FY 2025-26 centred on its integrated complex at Barwaha, near Indore, Madhya Pradesh — described as the country's largest integrated manufacturing facility at a single location. The headline project was the successful commissioning and stabilisation of a state-of-the-art Malt Spirit Plant of 6,000 LPD capacity at Barwaha, which strengthened backward integration and positioned the Company to participate in the premium and single malt whisky segment in the coming years; the Directors' Report attributes the year's higher depreciation to this Malt Plant being commissioned during the year. The grain-based Ethanol Plant of 130 KLPD capacity at Barwaha continued commercial operations, diversifying revenue streams and supporting the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme. The site also carries an ENA manufacturing capacity of 53 million litres per annum, an ethanol manufacturing capacity of 43 MLPA and 41 bottling lines with a collective capacity of 16 million cases per annum. Inorganically, the Company acted as Resolution Applicant in the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of SDF Industries Limited, Kerala; the resolution plan was approved by the Committee of Creditors and then by the NCLT Kochi Bench by order dated 16.04.2026, making SDF Industries a wholly owned subsidiary with the stated objective of expanding IMFL bottling capacity. Geographically, the footprint was extended across Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Goa, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, West Bengal and Manipur, with foundations laid for future growth in Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka in support of a pan-India integrated alcoholic beverage strategy. No rupee capex quantum is stated in the narrative chapters, and the named capital-commitment and segment-capital-expenditure disclosures supplied carried no readable figure with a printed unit.

risks.note: The MD&A's Industry Structure section notes the industry is strictly governed by state laws on production, distribution and marketing; licences and permits are required for manufacturing, bottling, storage, distribution and retail, and states may control distribution through government-owned entities or allow private distributors. Any change in a state's excise policy or licensing regime directly affects the Company's route to market.

risks.risk: Excise duty structure and the new 40% GST demerit rate on sin goods
risks.note: High inter-state duties prevail, requiring manufacturers to have multiple manufacturing units in different states of operation — a structural cost of geographic expansion. GST rate rationalisation introduced in September 2025 created a two-tier 5%/18% structure alongside a newly introduced 40% demerit rate for luxury and sin goods, raising the tax burden on the category.

risks.risk: Advertising and distribution restrictions limit brand-building levers
risks.note: Advertising restrictions, particularly above-the-line (ATL) advertising, limit marketing efforts, while hyper-local or on-demand online delivery is approved only in certain zones where state rules permit and online sales remain broadly restricted — constraining how a premiumisation strategy can be marketed and distributed.

risks.risk: GLP-1 medications and changing consumption behaviour as a structural volume headwind
risks.note: The MD&A explicitly flags GLP-1 drugs as creating 'an unexpected structural headwind for the alcohol industry' because they reduce alcohol cravings alongside food appetite; combined with Gen Z's more selective relationship with alcohol, this is described as a hurdle for alcohol volume growth, forcing reliance on premiumisation and low-alcohol launches to hold value.

risks.risk: Input cost inflation and raw material availability from geopolitical supply-chain disruption
risks.note: The Middle East war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz produced an energy crisis and severe supply chain disruptions; the FY 2026-27 outlook cites a sharp rise in crude oil prices and disrupted energy supply 'putting pressure on input costs and raw material availability'. Global headline inflation is projected to rise to 4.4% in 2026 with surging production and freight costs.

risks.risk: Agricultural / monsoon dependence and rural demand
risks.note: The Company's grain-based distillation depends on agricultural inputs, and the outlook states a deficient south-west monsoon is expected to impact agricultural activity and rural demand — a dual hit to grain cost and to the IMIL segment that primarily caters to the low-income rural segment.

risks.risk: Open competition-law proceedings (CCI investigation into IMIL supply)
risks.note: The Board's Report discloses that the CCI's Director General searched the registered office on 27 October 2021 to examine the supply and sale of IMIL products, and that a CCI order alleged cartelisation in IMIL supply; by order dated 20 March 2024 the CCI referred the investigation report back to the DG for further investigation, leaving the matter unresolved.

The Board's Report describes mitigations — firewall systems, genuine software applications, regular hardware updates, up-to-date antivirus solutions, employee training on cybersecurity best practices, a disaster recovery mechanism and a Digital Rights Management system — which identifies cyber threats to digital infrastructure as a risk management sees as live.

risks.risk: Concentration of manufacturing at a single integrated complex
risks.note: Production is centred on the integrated Barwaha manufacturing complex, where the new 6,000 LPD Malt Spirit Plant and the 130 KLPD grain-based ethanol plant sit; with high inter-state duties separately noted as requiring multiple units across states, single-site dependence is both an operating-disruption exposure and a limit on market access.

one-line thesis: AABL shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing in IMFL, driving 32% YoY volume growth in proprietary brands despite flattish top line; the strategic focus on proprietary portfolio, new product launches (RTD, tequila, single malt), and acquisition of SDF Industries to control bottling is positioning it as a future-ready premium alco-bev player with 50% revenue target from own brands in 5 years.
financial scorecard: revenue: flat YoY (INR1,000cr FY26) due to Inbrew transition; EBITDA/margin: +13% YoY to INR40cr (Q4), 17% margin (up 200 bps); PAT: +5% YoY to INR24cr (Q4), normalized PAT higher due to one-off Inbrew restructuring costs; order book: not disclosed; net debt: net debt-free
guidance: revenue growth: 10%+ YoY FY27; margin: 15% EBITDA margin target FY27; order inflow: none specified; capex/commissioning: INR10cr for SDF modernization, INR70cr total capex planned FY27 (includes SDF and malt facility ramp-up)
segment / subsidiary detail: Proprietary IMFL: 37% YoY volume growth to 6.6L cases, 38% revenue growth to INR50cr, 22% EBITDA margin (all-time high); IMFL (contract): revenue +7% YoY to INR62cr, 20% margin; Ethanol: volume -35% YoY to 4M liters, revenue INR24cr, 10% margin; Merchant ENA: volume +129% YoY to 6.9M liters, revenue +128% to INR47cr, 14% margin
growth verticals / optionality: RTD (Kultur) soft-launched in MP, label approvals pending in 14 states; tequila launch delayed to H1 FY27 due to shipping; single malt to launch H2 FY28 (FY29 full year); expansion into Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka; target 50% revenue from proprietary IMFL in 3-5 years
margins & cost dynamics: IMFL proprietary margin expected to normalize to 15-17% as premium marketing spends rise; packaging cost inflation (PET, paper, aluminum) mitigated via value engineering (e.g., removing mono cartons); ethanol margin at 7-10% EBITDA, not core but supports scale
capex / expansion: INR70cr total planned for FY27: INR30cr for SDF acquisition, INR10cr for SDF automation/modernization, remaining for malt facility scaling and bottling line upgrades
capital allocation: Prioritizing proprietary IMFL growth, backward integration (malt plant, bottling via SDF), and premium product launches; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; net debt-free position enables organic investment
risks & watch-items: Ethanol volume dependency on government blending policy (20%→25%); regulatory delays in RTD/tequila approvals; premium brand adoption lag in new states; packaging cost volatility; competition from Bacardi Breezer in RTD and established players in single malt
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, long-term oriented; clear focus on proprietary brands, operational control, and premiumization; transparent about challenges (ethanol, tequila delays); proactive on backward integration
non-obvious takeaways: SDF acquisition is not just about capacity—it’s a strategic geographic play (central Kerala location, proximity to airports) to solve bottling fragmentation and enable faster SKU rollout; single malt maturation already underway with blending exceeding expectations; ENA surplus is being cannibalized for own IMFL use, reducing external malt purchases

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Premiumization is the structural driver — consumers are trading up from mass-market to prestige, premium and luxury offerings on rising disposable incomes, urbanization, global exposure and social media influence
- Formalisation of the industry — the organized sector now controls approximately two-thirds of the Indian alcobev market by value, attributed to premiumization, stricter compliance, digital traceability and the exit of weaker informal players
- Headroom from low consumption — India's per capita alcohol consumption is nearly 5.5 litres against a global average of 6.2 litres; the Indian alcobev market was valued at $68.49 Billion in 2025 and is expected to reach $131 Billion by 2035 at 6.7% CAGR
- RTD and low-ABV formats gaining share — FSSAI amendments of 1 January 2026 formally recognised RTD as a category, easing regulatory approvals for low-ABV products and encouraging pre-mixed cocktail launches; nitro-infused beers were also assigned formal standards
- New consumer cohorts — a rising female consumer base, changing social norms and experiential/cocktail culture broadening the addressable occasion set
- Emerging distribution channels — home delivery and e-commerce gaining traction where state rules permit, though online sales remain broadly restricted
- GLP-1 medications are a structural headwind to alcohol volume growth as they reduce alcohol cravings; combined with Gen Z's more selective relationship with alcohol, players are countering through premiumization and low-alcohol launches
- Regulatory and tax structure remains the key constraint — state-specific excise regimes, exclusion of liquor from GST, high inter-state duties requiring multiple manufacturing units, ATL advertising restrictions, and a newly introduced 40% GST demerit rate for luxury and sin goods introduced in September 2025
- Macro outlook turning less supportive — India's real GDP growth is projected to decline to 6.6% in FY 2026-27 on Middle East war risk, with a sharp rise in crude prices, supply chain disruption pressuring input costs and raw material availability, and a deficient south-west monsoon expected to hit agricultural activity and rural demand
- Global growth is projected to slow to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 with headline inflation rising to 4.4% in 2026, pressuring production and freight costs
- Export optionality for Indian alcobev — APEDA targets scaling India's alcoholic beverage exports from ₹3,162.21 Crore to ₹8,535 Crore by 2030, though India currently ranks 40th worldwide in such exports

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: IMFL proprietary margin expected to normalize to 15-17% as premium marketing spends rise; packaging cost inflation (PET, paper, aluminum) mitigated via value engineering (e.g., removing mono cartons); ethanol margin at 7-10% EBITDA, not core but supports scale

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing proprietary IMFL growth, backward integration (malt plant, bottling via SDF), and premium product launches; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; net debt-free position enables organic investment

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: AABL's expansion during FY 2025-26 centred on its integrated complex at Barwaha, near Indore, Madhya Pradesh — described as the country's largest integrated manufacturing facility at a single location. The headline project was the successful commissioning and stabilisation of a state-of-the-art Malt Spirit Plant of 6,000 LPD capacity at Barwaha, which strengthened backward integration and positioned the Company to participate in the premium and single malt whisky segment in the coming years; the Directors' Report attributes the year's higher depreciation to this Malt Plant being commissioned during the year. The grain-based Ethanol Plant of 130 KLPD capacity at Barwaha continued commercial operations, diversifying revenue streams and supporting the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme. The site also carries an ENA manufacturing capacity of 53 million litres per annum, an ethanol manufacturing capacity of 43 MLPA and 41 bottling lines with a collective capacity of 16 million cases per annum. Inorganically, the Company acted as Resolution Applicant in the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of SDF Industries Limited, Kerala; the resolution plan was approved by the Committee of Creditors and then by the NCLT Kochi Bench by order dated 16.04.2026, making SDF Industries a wholly owned subsidiary with the stated objective of expanding IMFL bottling capacity. Geographically, the footprint was extended across Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Goa, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, West Bengal and Manipur, with foundations laid for future growth in Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka in support of a pan-India integrated alcoholic beverage strategy. No rupee capex quantum is stated in the narrative chapters, and the named capital-commitment and segment-capital-expenditure disclosures supplied carried no readable figure with a printed unit.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, strategic, long-term oriented; clear focus on proprietary brands, operational control, and premiumization; transparent about challenges (ethanol, tequila delays); proactive on backward integration

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": "true", "note": "The Board's Report discloses a Competition Commission of India matter: the Director General conducted a search at the registered office on 27 October 2021 examining the supply and sale of the Company's IMIL products, and a CCI order alleging cartelisation in IMIL supply followed. The Company challenged the CCI's jurisdiction before the Delhi High Court and, on the court's direction, took the matter back to the CCI; by order dated 20 March 2024 the CCI referred the investigation report back to the DG for further investigation. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated presence across the entire liquor value chain — IMFL (proprietary and licensed), IMIL, ENA and ethanol — from a single location described as India's largest integrated manufacturing facility
- Scale of the Barwaha complex: 41 bottling lines with a collective 16 million cases per annum, 53 MLPA ENA and 43 MLPA ethanol capacity
- Portfolio of 16 proprietary brands alongside an IMFL franchise arrangement with Diageo and contract manufacturing for United Spirits Limited (Diageo) and Inbrew
- Backward integration strengthened by the newly commissioned 6,000 LPD malt spirit plant, positioning the Company for the premium and single malt whisky segment
- Product innovation credential — accredited as the first in the world to manufacture white brandy
- Proprietary IMFL momentum — proprietary brand revenues grew approximately 29% and proprietary IMFL volumes grew 32% during the year, reflecting brand acceptance across key markets
- Participation in the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme diversifies revenue streams beyond beverage alcohol

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Ethanol volume dependency on government blending policy (20%→25%); regulatory delays in RTD/tequila approvals; premium brand adoption lag in new states; packaging cost volatility; competition from Bacardi Breezer in RTD and established players in single malt

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: SDF acquisition is not just about capacity—it’s a strategic geographic play (central Kerala location, proximity to airports) to solve bottling fragmentation and enable faster SKU rollout; single malt maturation already underway with blending exceeding expectations; ENA surplus is being cannibalized for own IMFL use, reducing external malt purchases

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Remain focused on enhancing operational efficiency, expanding the market footprint, building proprietary brands and investing in strategic growth initiatives
- Grow the proprietary IMFL business — proprietary brand revenues grew approximately 29% and proprietary IMFL volumes 32% during the year on increasing brand acceptance
- Expand and strengthen the portfolio through focused investments in premium and value-added offerings across whisky, gin, vodka, rum and brandy
- Deepen backward integration via the commissioned 6,000 LPD Malt Spirit Plant at Barwaha, positioning the Company to participate in …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] SDF Industries acquired via an IBC resolution plan approved by NCLT Kochi on 16 April 2026 for Rs 30.85 Cr; it becomes a wholly owned subsidiary and brings Kerala bottling in-house.
- [Business model change] The Inbrew arrangement shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing, structurally reducing reported IMFL licensed volumes without an equivalent economic loss.
- [Segment headwind] Ethanol faces industry oversupply that management expects to persist for the rest of the financial year, and the segment reported an operating loss in Q1FY27.
- [Industry] Indian alco-bev market sized at INR 3,255 Bn in 2024 heading to INR 5,763 Bn by 2030P; premium & luxury alco-bev at INR 28,751 Cr in 2024 to INR 50,000 Cr by 2029E, with whisky over 70% of IMFL.
- [Leadership] Promoter-led board (Prasann Kumar Kedia MD, Anshuman Kedia WTD & CEO) supplemented by senior hires from Pernod Ricard India and United Spirits in sales and marketing.

one-line thesis: AABL shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing in IMFL, driving 32% YoY volume growth in proprietary brands despite flattish top line; the strategic focus on proprietary portfolio, new product launches (RTD, tequila, single malt), and acquisition of SDF Industries to control bottling is positioning it as a future-ready premium alco-bev player with 50% revenue target from own brands in 5 years.
financial scorecard: revenue: flat YoY (INR1,000cr FY26) due to Inbrew transition; EBITDA/margin: +13% YoY to INR40cr (Q4), 17% margin (up 200 bps); PAT: +5% YoY to INR24cr (Q4), normalized PAT higher due to one-off Inbrew restructuring costs; order book: not disclosed; net debt: net debt-free
guidance: revenue growth: 10%+ YoY FY27; margin: 15% EBITDA margin target FY27; order inflow: none specified; capex/commissioning: INR10cr for SDF modernization, INR70cr total capex planned FY27 (includes SDF and malt facility ramp-up)
segment / subsidiary detail: Proprietary IMFL: 37% YoY volume growth to 6.6L cases, 38% revenue growth to INR50cr, 22% EBITDA margin (all-time high); IMFL (contract): revenue +7% YoY to INR62cr, 20% margin; Ethanol: volume -35% YoY to 4M liters, revenue INR24cr, 10% margin; Merchant ENA: volume +129% YoY to 6.9M liters, revenue +128% to INR47cr, 14% margin
growth verticals / optionality: RTD (Kultur) soft-launched in MP, label approvals pending in 14 states; tequila launch delayed to H1 FY27 due to shipping; single malt to launch H2 FY28 (FY29 full year); expansion into Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka; target 50% revenue from proprietary IMFL in 3-5 years
margins & cost dynamics: IMFL proprietary margin expected to normalize to 15-17% as premium marketing spends rise; packaging cost inflation (PET, paper, aluminum) mitigated via value engineering (e.g., removing mono cartons); ethanol margin at 7-10% EBITDA, not core but supports scale
capex / expansion: INR70cr total planned for FY27: INR30cr for SDF acquisition, INR10cr for SDF automation/modernization, remaining for malt facility scaling and bottling line upgrades
capital allocation: Prioritizing proprietary IMFL growth, backward integration (malt plant, bottling via SDF), and premium product launches; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; net debt-free position enables organic investment
